reviews.review: Best to play with a friend but great game

Admittedly, I've never played this co-op so everything I say here is solely about single player.

It's a dope roguelite FPS game with a nice hefty variety of weapons, characters, and modifiers (read 'scrolls') to spice up the gameplay. Sure some of the characters are locked behind DLC, but given the decent pricing of the game plus everything going on sale pretty frequently, I'd say it's totally wurf. 

There are no characters that feel like they're copying each other gameplay-wise. Each character has a unique ability that can usually be used after some time has passed and a secondary lethal ability of some kind. For instance, Crown Prince (the cat) has an orb that he can toss out that locks enemies in place along with dealing damage that even works on bosses and a poisonous smoke grenade that lingers, and his gameplay is drastically different from Ao Bai (the dog with the bandana), who can dual-wield his weapons and a basic frag grenade that doesn't have any special bells or whistles, but deals high damage. And those two are different from my favorite Li (the fox shaman), who can toss out a fireball directly forward and summon meteors on enemies she can see. The varied gameplay of each hero gives me a good reason to try each one out and pay for the DLC.

Equally as varied are the firearms. You have 2 weapons slots with one always taken up by a pistol you cannot drop, but has infinite ammo. All weapons uses a different type of ammunition, from Normal, Large, and Special Ammo, which you will always find in spades from breakable pots, shops, and chests. Each weapon can also get modifiers from basic ones like increased damage at a reduced RoF to special shared traits that only activate if you have 2 weapons with that trait, such as dealing massive damage by planting spores on the enemy by hitting them enough times.

During each run, you also earn gold, which is used for in-run purchases such as health, new weapons, ammo, and upgrading your weapon's level, and souls, which can be used for a once-per-run self revive and permanent upgrades. These upgrades can include things like additional held ammo, bonus crit chance, and even character-specific enhancements that can help alter their gameplay and make them more powerful.

The simple graphics make this game pretty easy on the eyes and will undoubtedly age very well into the future. If you're someone who loves to play games like Warframe and don't mind that the maps are basically like that ('tiles' that are shifted around and mixed up), then this is a very solid purchase.

8.7/10 - This score is really just my opinion on the single-player mode. Very possible it's even better with a team!
